limits: One fixed owned arithmetic function and one arithmetic-operator replacement family; no result is extrapolated to arbitrary applications.
Two native runs use fresh temporary directories on the same host with the same built Mewt and compiler bytes. This is normalized execution repeatability, not independently reproduced builds or hosts.
Direct mutant replays use the same pinned GCC compiler as the Mewt campaigns; they independently invoke the owned worker, not an independent compiler implementation.
The C++ grammar generates mutations for a function in the C/C++ common subset; tests compile that function as freestanding C11 with an owned Linux x86-64 entry point.
The kit pins copied GCC, linker and shared-library bytes plus the host ELF loader. The host Python interpreter, kernel and unshare utility are required and are not covered by that pinned closure.
No external target, arbitrary command, network runtime, autonomous intrusion or new vulnerability discovery is exercised.
Mewt declares AGPL-3.0. Its notice is retained; compatibility and obligations for commercial redistribution of the complete product and transitive dependencies remain unassessed here.
